question: Which exact P65 app/launcher/LVX API candidates could support a Canopus Manager backend, and where do they differ from the current LVGL v9 backend?
candidate_symbols: app_install candidate: 0x0C2418AC; observed R0 descriptor, R1 page-pointer array, R2 page count; return semantics not validated
app_launcher_add candidate: 0x0C7EC450; IDA pseudocode shows no explicit arguments; implementation reaches launcher-page insertion
P65 app/launcher removal candidate: 0x0C7EC53C; observed int(app_id), removes launcher icon and unlinks the app record; cleanup scope is not reconciled with app_install
P65 activity page-unregister candidate: 0x0C22212C; observed one page-descriptor pointer and lifecycle callback dispatch; public call/lifetime contract is unapproved
launcher_page_insert_icon candidate: 0x0C7F070C; observed one pointer argument for a launcher item
lvx_page_title_create candidate: 0x0C21B2FC; observed five arguments and pointer return
lvx_list_item_set_icon candidate: 0x0C219878; observed two arguments; not equivalent to the required row create/update API
lvx_list_refresh_to_bottom candidate: 0x0C8BD798 / Thumb callable 0x0C8BD799; one list-object pointer, AP trampoline to ROM 0x1C148888; scroll helper only, not row creation/update
P65 LVX list initializer candidate: 0x0C2401D4; caller supplies a native list object and the initializer installs a 40-byte config/callback table

P65 LVX list class-constructor callback candidate: 0x0C23FF40; raw code ignores R0, uses R1 as the list object, initializes state through +1356; shape is consistent with a class constructor callback, but class registration/public entrypoint is unproven
LVGL class-create candidate: 0x0C0D15D4; `(class_descriptor, parent)->object`, allocates from descriptor instance size and attaches to parent/display; not list-specific
LVGL class constructor-dispatch candidate: 0x0C0D16C8; walks class ancestry and calls each class+4 callback as `(class_descriptor, object)`; list descriptor linkage remains unknown
LVGL class destructor-dispatch candidate: 0x0C0D17D4; walks class ancestry and calls each class+8 destructor callback; list destructor callback remains unidentified
P65 LVX list config-copy helper candidate: 0x0C2358C4; code copies 10 words to list+92 after validating required callbacks; function-boundary/public ABI status remains unapproved

P65 LVX list create/config/finalize candidates: 0x0C8BE008 (parent, opaque descriptor) -> object, 0x0C8BEF60 (object, 40-byte callback table), and 0x0C8BEBC0 (object); AP trampolines to ROM 0x1C14885C/0x1C145B00/0x1C147054
P65 LVGL object-class create candidate: 0x0C8BEB70 / Thumb 0x0C8BEB71; observed `(class_descriptor, parent)->object` calls, including the P65 `listview` row class descriptor at VMA 0x3C21B55C
P65 LVGL label-child create candidate: 0x0C78BCB4 / Thumb 0x0C78BCB5; one parent pointer, creates a child from label descriptor VMA 0x3C224844
P65 LVGL label text-set candidate: 0x0C78C878 / Thumb 0x0C78C879; int(label, const char *), updates the label-owned text buffer at +52
P65 LVGL event-callback registration candidate: 0x0C8BCE78 / Thumb 0x0C8BCE79; (object, callback, event_code, context), used for click event 7 in row creation

P65 all-list callback candidates: key/type 0x0C763B84, row create 0x0C764638, row update 0x0C7644A0, count 0x0C763B34; concrete all_list_view registration/call-site confirms the callback roles but its context uses P65-specific all_list records
P65 LVX row-item constructor-like candidate: 0x0C219454; seven arguments, returns the caller-provided item object after setting up child-object fields; direct public call path is unproven
P65 LVX row-item update candidate: 0x0C2196F8; six arguments, mutates existing item child/style state; relationship to list callback +104 is unproven
lvx_notification_insert_message candidate: 0x0CA60098; observed one pointer argument; not required for initial Manager UI
NuttX open wrapper candidate: 0x0C247EA8 / Thumb callable 0x0C247EA9; int(const char *, int, ...)
NuttX close wrapper candidate: 0x0C244B60 / Thumb callable 0x0C244B61; int(int fd)
NuttX read wrapper candidate: 0x0C2484E4 / Thumb callable 0x0C2484E5; int32_t(int fd, void *buffer, uint32_t count)
NuttX write wrapper candidate: 0x0C248454 / Thumb callable 0x0C248455; int32_t(int fd, const void *buffer, uint32_t count)
NuttX register_driver trampoline candidate: 0x0C8BD0D0 / Thumb callable 0x0C8BD0D1; int(const char *path, const file_operations *, mode_t, void *priv)
callsite_evidence: AP startup copy maps the 0x3C name-data VMA back to cached XIP. The `app_install` name at runtime VMA 0x3C350B00 maps to source/XIP 0x0C4408C4; the `launcher_page_insert_icon` name at 0x3C23F2F4 maps to XIP 0x0C3500B8; the `app_launcher_add` name at 0x3C23E7F0 maps to XIP 0x0C3505B4; and `lvx_page_title_create` at 0x3C2A3300 maps to XIP 0x0C3930C4. Literal-pool references in AP code connect these names to the candidate functions below.

Code at 0x0C2418AC was not auto-created as a function in the original IDB; a temporary in-memory function boundary was added for inspection, without saving the IDB. Its Thumb prologue saves R0/R1/R2 as descriptor, page-pointer array, and page count. It checks duplicate app IDs, allocates and copies 16 descriptor words (64 bytes), duplicates selected string fields, inserts the app into the 0x3C3CF91C registry, and registers page pointers. The argument shape and 64-byte copy match the current LVGL v9 `firmware_app_descriptor`; exact return semantics and all page-lifetime rules remain unverified.

Page-unregister candidate 0x0C22212C is reached by the `activitymanager_page_unregister` name string. Its code reads lifecycle state at page+40, calls the signal callback at +52 with event codes 6/7/2, indirect-dispatches callbacks at +92/+96, and unlinks page registry links at +64/+68. These offsets resemble the Band 10 page descriptor, but the routine has no direct AP callers and no `app_install` teardown path is linked to it.

The `app_launcher_add` name pointer is read in the literal pool preceding 0x0C7EC53C; the associated routine at 0x0C7EC450 obtains an app/launcher object, calls 0x0C7F070C, and updates launcher registries. Code references from 0x0C82FCDC (after an app-registry append) and 0x0C8B3BA8 (an app-launch path) invoke it with no arguments. It therefore appears to be a launcher-refresh helper, unlike the Band 10 v9 backend's `launcher_add(uint16_t)` wrapper; do not reuse that prototype or treat it as a direct add-by-app-ID API.

The NuttX registration trampoline at 0x0C8BD0D0 is a short Thumb stub to ROM 0x1C15A954. P65 driver code calls it with path, a file-operations table, mode 0x1B6, and a private pointer; the HYN/other driver init paths check its return. This matches `register_driver(path,fops,mode,priv)` at the call boundary, but the ROM implementation and a matching unregister API have not been recovered.

`launcher_page_insert_icon` is referenced from the function at 0x0C7EC450 and resolves to 0x0C7F070C. The recovered routine takes one record pointer and uses global launcher state at 0x3C456FA0; this is not the same observed ABI as Band 10's app-ID launcher-add call.

`lvx_page_title_create` resolves to 0x0C21B2FC. Its decompilation and four exact P65 caller sites show five arguments; callers pass `(page/root, title, mode, callback-or-resource, context)`. This arity matches the five-argument typedef in `manager/target/lvgl_v9/canopus_manager_target_lvgl_v9.c`, but callback ownership and the rest of the descriptor ABI still require review.

`lvx_list_item_set_icon` resolves to 0x0C219878 and decompiles as a two-argument item operation. Its P65 implementation reads an item subobject at `item + 84`; the exact Band 10 `.036` evidence in `EVID-UI-001` records the same-named operation accessing `item + 52`, so the list-item layouts are not interchangeable. The P65 strings do not expose the v9 backend's `LVX_LIST_ROW_CREATE`, `LVX_LIST_ROW_UPDATE`, or `LVX_LIST_ROW_TRAILING` names.

P65's LVX list path uses a native callback-driven object, distinct from the v9 row macros. The code at 0x0C2358C4 validates config words at +4/+8/+12/+20, then copies 40 bytes (10 words) into list-object offsets +92..+128; 0x0C2401D4 calls it with built-in ROM Thumb callback pointers: list+96=0x1C15015D, +100=0x1C15034D, +104=0x1C150591, +112=0x1C15016D, +116=0x1C1505E5, +120=0x1C1505F5; +108/+124/+128 are zero in this default table. Internal code proves these callback roles: +96 `(list,index,ctx)->key` (consumed as an 8-bit cache key), +100 `(list,index,ctx)->row object`, +104 `(list,row,index,ctx)->void` update, and +112 `(list,ctx)->item count`. In one concrete all-list configuration, +116/+120 are both bound to count-like `(list,ctx)->int` helpers; list-event code also invokes these slots in scroll-boundary branches and ignores their return. Their general semantics remain unknown. +124 replaces row-by-row total-extent measurement in `sub_C235F54`, and +128 supplies a geometry value to scrolling calculations in `sub_C235E6C`; +108 is copied but no use was found in the examined list routines. `sub_C2340C8`, `sub_C235B08`, and `sub_C233414` show the create/update paths. ROM callback bodies are outside this AP database. List class-constructor callback candidate 0x0C23FF40 ignores R0, uses R1 as the object, zeros fields +1340/+1344/+1348/+1352, sets word +1356 to 0x0101, registers a callback through helper 0x0C2570BC, and calls 0x0C255D24 with (object,200,0). This argument shape is consistent with a class constructor callback, but it has no direct AP caller/data xref or embedded AP function pointer, so LVX class registration/public creation remains unproven. Separately, `lv_obj_class_create_obj` string and behavior identify candidate 0x0C0D15D4: it allocates from class descriptor instance-size metadata at +32, stores class/parent pointers, and attaches the object to its parent/display. Candidate 0x0C0D16C8 walks the class chain and invokes +4 constructors as `(class,object)` base-to-derived; candidate 0x0C0D17D4 invokes +8 destructor callbacks in reverse order, after which deletion unlinks/frees the object. Wrapper 0x0C0E1B90 uses generic class descriptor VMA 0x3C1DE5C8 (source/XIP 0x0C2CE38C), whose name pointer resolves to `obj`; descriptor word +32 is 0x34A and the create path decodes its instance size as 0x34 (52 bytes). This is not the `lvx_list` descriptor. No list descriptor link to 0x0C23FF40 or matching +8 destructor was found. Raw AP scans found none of the absolute pointer aliases 0x0C23FF41, 0x2C23FF41, or 0x3C23FF41; the descriptor may be outside AP data or dynamically registered, but neither is proven. Other list code reads +1364, establishing only that the object layout extends at least through that byte; allocator/instance size/destructor are unknown. This recovers internal state and callback conventions, not a supported external API.

A concrete P65 all-list page at `sub_C764170` creates a list widget with ROM trampoline 0x0C8BE008(parent, opaque descriptor 0x3C19D9EC), builds the 40-byte callback table, calls 0x0C8BEF60(list, table), then finalizes through 0x0C8BEBC0(list). The table is `[ctx, sub_C763B84 key/type, sub_C764638 create, sub_C7644A0 update, 0, sub_C763B34 count, sub_C764598, sub_C7645E8, 0, 0]`. `sub_C764638` creates a P65 `listview` class row via ROM class-create trampoline 0x0C8BEB70 with descriptor 0x3C21B55C, then fills its child widgets; class descriptor name `listview` is at XIP 0x0C30B320 and its encoded base instance size is 76 bytes. It creates labels through 0x0C78BCB4 using descriptor 0x3C224844 (`label`), sets text through 0x0C78C878, and registers click handling through 0x0C8BCE78 with event code 7. The setter replaces/owns a text buffer at label+52. `sub_C7644A0` refreshes that row from the same P65 all_list record context. These callback conventions now have an exact firmware caller, but the callbacks depend on P65 all_list storage and are not directly reusable for Canopus snapshots. The opaque list descriptor, row widget layout, ownership and teardown remain unreviewed.

The exact P65 AP contains LVGL source-path strings under `apps/graphics/lvgl/lvgl/src/` plus LVX components including `lvx_widgets/lvx_list.c`. This suggests the v9 backend is worth investigating but does not prove its structure layout, version, or individual function ABIs match P65.

The row-item code has constructor-like candidate 0x0C219454 (`int(item, int, int, int, int, u8, u8)`), which returns the supplied object and conditionally creates child objects at offsets +84/+92/+96 after creating a related child at +88; it does not allocate the outer item. Update candidate 0x0C2196F8 (`int(item, int, int, int, int, char)`) accesses existing fields +84/+88/+92/+96. No direct code/data xrefs link either candidate to the list +100 create or +104 update callback, so this is a row-object candidate only, not recovered callback implementation.

The copied source string `lvx_list_refresh_to_bottom` is at 0x0C342324 (runtime VMA 0x3C252560). The exact caller `sub_C81B2B4` logs that function name and invokes AP Thumb trampoline 0x0C8BD799 (even entry 0x0C8BD798), which jumps to ROM 0x1C148888 with one list-object pointer. It is a scroll-to-bottom helper candidate only; it does not expose list construction or row callbacks.

Removal is partially mapped: `sub_C830114` (quickapp_unregister_app source name) reads the app id at record+16 and calls 0x0C7EC53C. That routine calls launcher-icon removal 0x0C7F077C, unlinks the app from launcher registries, and frees its app record. Separately, `activitymanager_page_unregister` maps to 0x0C22212C, whose code manipulates page lifecycle state and indirect-dispatches page callbacks. No exact callsite ties page unregister to `app_install` teardown, and callback draining/order are unknown; do not call these from Manager unload yet.

The P65 AP includes source strings `vfs/fs_open.c` (file offset 0x2E0BF0), `vfs/fs_close.c` (0x2E0B64), and `vfs/fs_read.c` (0x2E0C10). The low-level file-object open dispatcher is at 0x0C247AE8/0x0C247C64; file-object close is at 0x0C24605C; read/write inode-op dispatchers are at 0x0C2484E4/0x0C248454. These internal routines are distinct from the fd-facing wrappers below.

The P65 `open` wrapper candidate at 0x0C247EA8 calls the internal file-open routine with the path, flags and optional mode, then allocates a task file descriptor; errors set errno and return -1. Exact P65 AP callers pass pathname strings plus flags/mode, consistent with a POSIX `open` wrapper.

The candidate `close` wrapper at 0x0C244B60 indexes the current task file table using the integer argument, adjusts file references, closes the underlying file when the last reference is released, and returns success/error. It is distinct from internal file-object close at 0x0C24605C.

Raw Thumb disassembly for `read` at 0x0C2484E4 preserves R1 as the buffer and R2 as the byte count, resolves R0 as the fd, and dispatches through the inode read op at offset +8; it returns the byte count or -1 with errno. `write` at 0x0C248454 resolves the fd and dispatches to the inode write op at offset +12 with the supplied buffer/count.

The supervisor still needs NuttX `register_driver`/`unregister_driver` plus several LVX methods. A P65 AP search found no `unregister_driver` name/string or verified callable; the Band 10 lead 0x0C1B002C is not transferable because that P65 address is inside `sub_C1AFFF4` arithmetic/indexed-store code. This rules out the cross-target address only; the P65 register stub jumps to ROM and an unmapped ROM unregister counterpart remains possible. Open/close/read/write alone do not make the service operational.

IDA provenance caveat: the first-pass IDB hash was 4d2eb1c18f4a14dd27c07482105f76c06d5ab9c057745aef132da34516bcc6e5, but the current on-disk `.i64` hash is 6c2c3ac059a1b32f243573fda1aa16050e8b0c50332fdd6389203c3db852fd59. The AP payload SHA remains a19b601477569765103eaf468b937bd8026b4d68ffa5c896bde222a79e475858; use raw payload bytes as the firmware identity. The unregister negative scan used a temporary copy of the current database.
unsafe_assumptions: Names recovered through the startup data-copy map and matching behavior do not by themselves prove a callable ABI, ownership, thread safety, or acceptable side effects.

The P65 64-byte app descriptor copy matches the size/layout used by the current v9 backend, but the page descriptor layout, unregister path, duplicate-install behavior, and return-value semantics are not yet reconciled end-to-end. `app_launcher_add` is not an app-ID function in the recovered P65 code; app registration may trigger launcher refresh asynchronously, but that event/lifecycle relation has not been proven.
P65 `app_launcher_add` and `launcher_page_insert_icon` are not interchangeable with the Band 10 `launcher_add(app_id)` API based on current evidence.

The P65 and Band 10 `.036` `lvx_list_item_set_icon` implementations touch different item offsets (+84 versus +52), and P65's list callbacks reside in a different native object layout; do not transplant the Band 10 list backend layout into P65. The newly recovered callback prototypes are internal evidence only and are not yet safe target callables.

The file-I/O wrappers look POSIX-shaped and their machine-level argument flow is statically traced, but no host module or device call has tested them. A register_driver trampoline candidate is found, but its ROM body and matching unregister_driver API remain unreviewed; several LVX list-row functions are still unlocated. A few LVX function-name matches do not provide the full API set required by the Manager. Do not set `CANOPUS_SUP_PLATFORM_COMPLETE=1`, add callables, or build a deployable P65 Manager from these candidates.
recommended_probe: Continue exact P65 IDA analysis to locate the LVX list class descriptor/registration and its +8 destructor callback (raw AP scans contain no absolute pointer alias to 0x0C23FF40), recover native list allocation/teardown, connect +100/+104 to row factory/updater candidates, and identify any trailing/status-row equivalent. Trace `lvx_list_refresh_to_bottom` only as a scroll helper, then pursue app lookup/idempotence, launcher insertion/removal semantics, register_driver/unregister_driver, and NuttX error/thread constraints. Compare prototypes and ownership rules against the LVGL v9 backend before creating any target-specific config. Keep the production build gate closed and perform no device calls.
